__inputs.name: DS_CLOUD_MONITORING
__inputs.label: Google Cloud Monitoring
__inputs.description: Cloud Monitoring with roles/monitoring.viewer on the project

title: SQL Server on Google Cloud SQL — mssql-exporter + Cloud Monitoring
description: Engine metrics from mssql-exporter (Prometheus) next to host metrics from Google Cloud Monitoring (cloudsql.googleapis.com). Pick the Cloud SQL instance and the exporter's sqlserver_instance separately.

list.name: cloudsql_instance
list.label: Cloud SQL instance (Cloud Monitoring)
list.description: database_id of the Cloud SQL instance (<project>:<instance>).

list.name: sqlserver_instance
list.label: sqlserver_instance (exporter)
list.description: Set instance_label in the exporter to keep this name stable.

panels.title: SQL Server
panels.description: sqlserver_up from the exporter: 1 when the exporter can reach SQL Server.

panels.title: Current host
panels.description: @@SERVERNAME of the instance answering on the private IP. On Cloud SQL it is a generated host name (SQL Server runs on Linux); set instance_label to keep the sqlserver_instance label stable.

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: SQL Server keeps most of the memory for its buffer pool, so high usage is normal; compare with page life expectancy.

panels.title: Disk used
panels.description: Share of the provisioned disk in use. With storage auto-increase on, Cloud SQL grows the disk before it fills.

panels.title: Oldest last FULL backup
panels.description: Age of the oldest 'last FULL backup' across databases. Cloud SQL records its automated backups in msdb: FULL backups and, with point-in-time recovery on, LOG backups every 5 minutes.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: SQL Server reserves most of the memory for its buffer pool, so usage close to the quota is normal; compare with page life expectancy below.

panels.title: Disk usage
panels.description: Cloud Monitoring has no disk latency or queue depth for Cloud SQL; use io_file_stats stalls from the exporter for latency.

panels.title: Instance up (Cloud Monitoring)
panels.description: 1 while Cloud SQL considers the instance up. Compare with sqlserver_up in the overview, which is the exporter's view through the private IP.

panels.title: Disk writes (Cloud Monitoring) vs SQL Server file writes (exporter)
panels.description: The disk also absorbs writes SQL Server files do not account for (Cloud SQL backups and agents), so the Cloud Monitoring line is usually higher.

panels.title: Connections (Cloud Monitoring) vs user connections (exporter)
panels.description: Cloud Monitoring counts every connection, including the ones Cloud SQL itself opens (CloudDbSqlRoot, CloudDbSqlAgent).

panels.title: Engine — exporter vs Cloud Monitoring (same counters)
Batch requests/s
panels.description: Cloud SQL publishes some SQL Server counters itself; the two lines should overlap. A gap points to a scrape or alignment problem.

panels.title: Page life expectancy
panels.description: Cloud SQL publishes some SQL Server counters itself; the two lines should overlap. A gap points to a scrape or alignment problem.

panels.title: Deadlocks/s
panels.description: Cloud SQL publishes some SQL Server counters itself; the two lines should overlap. A gap points to a scrape or alignment problem.

panels.title: Top waits (ms/s)
panels.description: Wait time accumulated per second by wait type (sys.dm_os_wait_stats). Idle/background waits (lazy writer, checkpoint, queue and timer waits, HADR housekeeping) are excluded here; HADR_SYNC_COMMIT and other waits that slow queries are kept.

panels.title: Top queries (by CPU)
panels.description: Requires the top_queries collector (and include_text for the statement).

defaults.noValue: top_queries collector disabled or no data

panels.title: Index fragmentation (most fragmented)
panels.description: Requires the index_fragmentation collector. On Cloud SQL, create a user for the exporter login in each database to read (CONNECT ANY DATABASE and ##MS_DatabaseConnector## cannot be granted).

defaults.noValue: index_fragmentation collector disabled or not collected yet

panels.title: Time since last backup
panels.description: Cloud SQL automated backups: FULL backups and, with point-in-time recovery on, LOG backups every 5 minutes, including the internal gcloud_cloudsqladmin database.

panels.title: Log used (%) by database
panels.description: Includes the internal gcloud_cloudsqladmin database.
Cloud SQL read replicas (Enterprise edition) use read-scale availability groups. Empty without replicas: the high-availability standby is a regional disk, not an AG.
panels.title: Always On replicas (read replicas)

panels.description: Per database replica: synchronization state, suspension, lag and queues. Queues are absent while data movement is suspended (SQL Server reports NULL). Aggregated across every exporter in the AG (a secondary only sees its own replica), so the instance selector does not apply here.
panels.title: Always On databases (read replicas)
Log Reuse Wait
panels.description: Why each database's transaction log cannot be truncated (sys.databases.log_reuse_wait_desc). LOG_BACKUP is normal for FULL recovery between log backups. AVAILABILITY_REPLICA = a lagging AG secondary, REPLICATION = CDC or replication, ACTIVE_TRANSACTION = a long-open transaction. Refreshed by SQL Server on truncation attempts (checkpoint / log backup), so it can lag a few minutes and stay stale on idle databases: read it together with Log Used (%).

panels.title: Log Held (non-routine reasons)
panels.description: Periods when a database's log could not be truncated for a reason other than NOTHING, LOG_BACKUP or CHECKPOINT (e.g. AVAILABILITY_REPLICA, REPLICATION, ACTIVE_TRANSACTION). Alert on it together with Log Used (%), see the README.

defaults.noValue: No log held by a non-routine reason

panels.title: State Differs From Configured
panels.description: Databases whose Query Store actual state differs from the configured one, typically READ_ONLY after it filled up: it silently stops capturing. On a readable AG secondary READ_ONLY (reason 8) is expected. Requires the opt-in query_store collector (--collector.query_store).

defaults.noValue: query_store collector disabled or not collected yet

panels.title: Capture Stopped by a Limit
panels.description: Databases whose Query Store is READ_ONLY because it reached a limit (readonly_reason >= 65536: max storage size, statement count, in-memory or database size limit). Raise MAX_STORAGE_SIZE_MB or tune the cleanup policy, then set it back to READ_WRITE.

defaults.noValue: query_store collector disabled or not collected yet

panels.title: Failing Forced Plans
panels.description: Forced plans whose forcing has failed (force_failure_count > 0, e.g. the plan uses an index that was dropped): the query runs with another plan. See last_force_failure_reason_desc in sys.query_store_plan.

defaults.noValue: query_store collector disabled or not collected yet

panels.title: Last Collection
panels.description: Age and result of the last background Query Store collection (default every 5m). FAILED means at least one database failed; the error is in the exporter log.

defaults.noValue: query_store collector disabled or not collected yet

panels.title: Query Store by Database
panels.description: Query Store health per database. Requires the opt-in query_store collector; databases the login cannot access are skipped (see the README permissions).

defaults.noValue: query_store collector disabled or not collected yet

panels.title: Query Store Storage Used (%)
panels.description: Space used by Query Store relative to MAX_STORAGE_SIZE_MB. At 100% it switches to READ_ONLY and stops capturing.

defaults.noValue: query_store collector disabled or not collected yet
